proof.text: Write $j_U^*$ for restriction of module sheaves to the localized ringed site and put $F=j_U^*\circ c_J:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(\underline R|_U)$. The constant module functor is additive and exact by [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor]; module restriction is additive and exact by [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction]. Their composite is therefore additive and exact. Applying the two termwise representative comparisons gives $c(QK)|_U\cong Q(FK)$ for every, possibly unbounded, complex $K$ of $R$-modules. These comparisons are natural in chain maps. Here $F(T)=\underline T|_U$ and no connectedness of $U$ is required.

proof.text: For a representative complex $K$ and any $i\in\mathbf Z$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to the exact functor $F$ of step 1. It gives the canonical comparison $H^i(FK)\cong F(H^i(K))$, induced by the preserved kernel and image of the differentials and natural in chain maps. The representative comparison in step 1 and the cohomology factorization through $Q$ in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] consequently give $H^i(c(QK)|_U)\cong\underline{H^i(QK)}|_U$. Every derived object has a complex representative, so this constructs the asserted isomorphism on objects in all degrees.

proof.text: The comparisons in step 2 are natural for all derived morphisms, not only for chain maps: by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $D(R)$ is the localization at quasi-isomorphisms. Naturality holds for the image $Q(a)$ of each chain map $a$. For a quasi-isomorphism $s$, both functors in the comparison send $Q(s)$ to an isomorphism, so multiplying its naturality square by these inverses proves naturality for $Q(s)^{-1}$. Composing squares proves naturality for every composite of these generators, hence for every morphism of the localization. This also makes the comparison independent of a chosen representative up to the canonical comparison isomorphisms. In particular $H^i(c(f)|_U)$ corresponds to $F(H^i(f))$.

proof.text: Now suppose $c(f)|_U$ is an isomorphism and fix $i\in\mathbf Z$. Applying the functor $H^i$ to an inverse shows that $H^i(c(f)|_U)$ is an isomorphism; by step 3, so is $F(g)$, where $g=H^i(f)$. Part (a) of [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology], applied to the exact functor $F$, identifies $F(\ker g)$ with $\ker F(g)=0$ and $F(\operatorname{coker}g)$ with $\operatorname{coker}F(g)=0$. Thus $\underline{\ker g}|_U$ and $\underline{\operatorname{coker}g}|_U$ are zero module sheaves. Apply [lem-sfb-constant-realization-detects-zero] separately to the two $R$-modules $\ker g$ and $\operatorname{coker}g$. Its nonemptiness hypothesis is precisely the hypothesis on $U$ in the statement; it gives $\ker g=0$ and $\operatorname{coker}g=0$. The first equality says $g$ is injective, while the second says every target element is an image. Hence $g$ is a bijective linear map, whose inverse is linear, and is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Step 4 proves that $H^i(f)$ is an isomorphism for every integer $i$. The criterion [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology], applied to the abelian category $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$, now gives that $f$ is an isomorphism in $D(R)$. This criterion is explicitly unbounded. All preceding exactness and detection statements apply to arbitrary modules over any commutative ring, so the argument introduces no finiteness, Noetherian, or boundedness assumption.

title: Constant realization reflects algebraic derived isomorphisms locally
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $U\to X$ be a nonempty object of its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $R$ be a commutative ring. Use constant module sheaves [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor] and the derived constant realization $c:D(R)\to D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\underline R)$ [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor], where the derived categories and module sheaves are [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For every $C\in D(R)$ and integer $i$, there is a natural isomorphism $H^i(c(C)|_U)\cong\underline{H^i(C)}|_U$. For every morphism $f:C\to D$ in $D(R)$, if $c(f)|_U$ is an isomorphism in the derived category on the localized ringed site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], then $f$ is an isomorphism in $D(R)$. Here $\underline R$ and $\underline{H^i(C)}$ are the constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. No boundedness, finite-generation, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.
